'''Gheorghe Moroșanu''' (born April 30, 1950, in [[Darabani]], [[Botoșani County]], [[Romania]]) is a Romanian mathematician known for his publications in Ordinary Differential Equations, Partial Differential Equations, Nonlinear Analysis, Calculus of Variations, Fluid Mechanics, Asymptotic Analysis, Applied Mathematics. 
He earned his Ph.D. in 1981 from the [[Alexandru Ioan Cuza University]] in  [[Iași]], [[Romania]].

He is currently affiliated with the [[Babeș-Bolyai University]] in [[Cluj-Napoca]], [[Romania]]. Between 2002 and 2020 he was a professor at the [[Central European University]] in  [[Budapest]] (an international English-language  university, accredited in the USA), after previously holding positions at the [[University of Stuttgart]] and ''Alexandru Ioan Cuza'' University of Iași, Romania.

Among several administrative positions, he served as chairman of the Mathematics Department of the Central European University in Budapest since 2004 to 2012. In 2008 he was appointed as ''egyetemi tanár'' (the highest academic title in Hungarian higher education) by the President of Hungary.<ref>{{citation|title= Határozata egyetemi tanári kinevezésekről (in English: Decision on appointments of university professors)|journal=Oktatási Közlöny |volume=52 |issue=22 |date=14 August 2008|page=2490}}</ref><ref>[http://www.kozlonyok.hu/kozlonyok/Kozlonyok/21/PDF/2008/22.pdf Gheorghe Moroșanu appointed as ''egyetemi tanár'' by the President of Hungary (László Sólyom); see page 2490], retrieved April 1, 2015</ref>

Before his university studies, during the 12-year period of education from primary to high school (1957–1969), Gheorghe Moroșanu was at the top of his class each academic year and demonstrated a keen interest in mathematics.

In 1969 he started studying mathematics at the ''Alexandru Ioan Cuza'' University in Iaşi. He was the first to earn a Ph.D. of his class of over 150 graduates. His PhD thesis, entitled ''Qualitative Problems for Nonlinear Differential Equations of Accretive Type in Banach Spaces'',<ref>{{MathGenealogy|76848}}</ref> included original results published in top-ranked journals, such as ''Atti della Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei, Journal of Differential Equations, Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications, Nonlinear Analysis, Numerical Functional Analysis and Optimization''. In particular, Gheorghe Moroșanu solved in his thesis the problem of the existence and uniqueness of the solution of a hyperbolic differential system with some ''nonlocal boundary conditions'',<ref>{{citation
  | last1=Moroșanu |first1=G.
  | title = On a class of nonlinear differential hyperbolic systems with nonlocal boundary conditions
  | journal = J. Differential Equations
  | pages = 43 (1982) 345–368}}</ref> thus correcting a paper by Viorel Barbu and Ioan I. Vrabie,<ref>{{citation
 | title = An existence result for a nonlinear boundary-value problem of hyperbolic type
 | journal = Nonlinear Analysis
 | pages =  1 (1976/77) 373–382
 | last1 = Barbu
 | first1 = Viorel
 | last2 = Vrabie
 | first2 = Ioan I.}}</ref> which actually does not cover the case of nonlocal boundary conditions, in contrast to what those authors asserted.

Gheorghe Moroșanu is the author and co-author of a large number of research articles and several books (monographs and textbooks).

His monograph on nonlinear evolution equations<ref>{{citation|first1=G. |last1=Moroșanu |title=Nonlinear Evolution Equations and Applications|date=31 August 1988 |publisher=D. Reidel Publishing Co., Dordrecht-Boston-Lancaster-Tokyo, 1988|isbn=978-90-277-2486-1}}</ref> is mainly focused on the stability theory for such equations. In the preface of this monograph, Professor [[Michiel Hazewinkel]] (Series Editor) states that <blockquote> ''the theory of stability of ordinary differential equations contains the germs for a theory of stability of nonlinear evolution semigroups ... This book is devoted to a self-contained systematic exposition of these matters and incorporates many of the author's own substantial results in the field''. </blockquote> This book has been followed by a series of related papers, including his articles on second-order evolution equations governed by monotone operators.<ref>{{citation
  | last1=Moroșanu |first1=G.
  | title = Second-order differential equations on R+ governed by monotone operators
  | journal = Nonlinear Analysis
  | pages = 83 (2013) 69–81}}</ref><ref>{{citation
  | last1=Moroșanu |first1=G.
  | title = Existence results for second-order monotone differential inclusions on the positive half-line
  | journal = Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications
  | pages = 419 (2014) 94–113
 }}</ref><ref>{{citation
  | last1 = Moroşanu| first1 = G.
  | title = Existence for second order differential inclusions on R+ governed by monotone operators
  | journal = Advanced Nonlinear Studies
  | pages = 14 (2014) 661–670}}</ref><ref>{{citation
  | last1=Moroșanu |first1=G.
  | title = On a class of second-order differential inclusions on the positive half-line
  | journal = Zeitschrift für Analysis und Ihre Anwendungen
  | pages = 34 (2015) 17–26}}</ref> These publications provide a complete answer to the long-standing existence question in the non-homogeneous case.

Both his joint monograph on functional methods<ref>{{citation|first1=V.-M. |last1=Hokkanen |first2=G.|last2=Moroșanu |title=Functional Methods in Differential Equations|date=26 April 2002 |publisher=Chapman and Hall/CRC, Boca Raton-London-New York-Washington, D.C., 2002|isbn=978-1-58488-283-1}}</ref> and that on singular perturbations<ref>{{citation |first1=L. |last1=Barbu |first2=G. |last2=Moroșanu |title=Singularly Perturbed Boundary-Value Problems|date=28 June 2007 |publisher=Birkhäuser, Basel-Boston-Berlin, 2007 |isbn=978-3-7643-8330-5}}</ref> contain original material mostly due to the authors, bringing new ideas and methods that are useful in exploring mathematical models described by linear and nonlinear differential equations. In particular the book on singular perturbations combines results from different parts of mathematics to offer a detailed asymptotic analysis of some important classes of singularly perturbed boundary value problems which are mathematical models for various phenomena in biology, chemistry, engineering. This book has been followed by some related joint papers on abstract semilinear and fully nonlinear evolution equations with significant applications.<ref>{{citation
 | title = Elliptic-like regularization of semilinear evolution equations
 | journal = Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications
 | pages = 396 (2012) 759–771
 | last1 = Ahsan
 | first1 = M.
 | last2 = Moroşanu
 | first2 = G.
 }}</ref><ref>{{citation
 | title = Asymptotic expansions for elliptic-like regularizations of semilinear evolution equations
 | journal = Journal of Differential Equations
 | pages = 257 (2014) 2926–2949
 | last1 = Ahsan
 | first1 = M.
 | last2 = Moroșanu
 | first2 = G.
 }}</ref><ref>{{citation
 | title = Elliptic-like regularization of semilinear evolution equations and applications to some hyperbolic problems
 | journal = Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications
 | pages =  449 (2017) 966–978
 | last1 = Barbu
 | first1 = L.
 | last2 = Moroşanu
 | first2 = G.
 }}</ref><ref>{{citation
 | title = Elliptic-like regularization of a fully nonlinear evolution inclusion and applications
 | journal = Communications in Contemporary Mathematics
 | pages=19, 1650037 (2017)
 | last1 = Barbu
 | first1 = L.
 | last2 = Moroşanu
 | first2 = G.
 }}</ref>

In 2019, he published a book on functional analysis,<ref>{{citation|first1=G. |last1=Moroșanu |title=Functional Analysis for the Applied Sciences|date=28 December 2019 |publisher=Springer, Cham, Switzerland, 2019|isbn=978-3-030-27152-7}}</ref> which consists of a mixture of standard functional analysis tools and real world problems.

Gheorghe Moroșanu has also works in Calculus of Variations, Fluid Mechanics, etc. More specifically, his legacy of contributions concerns (but is not limited to) the following topics:

* first and second-order evolution equations in Hilbert spaces;
* initial-boundary value problems for parabolic and hyperbolic partial differential equations and systems (existence, high regularity, stability of solutions, time periodic solutions);
* singular perturbation theory for nonlinear partial differential equations and semilinear evolution equations in Hilbert spaces;
* boundary value problems for elliptic equations, including equations involving p-Laplacians, related eigenvalue problems;
* nonlinear ordinary differential equations, integro-differential equations, delay differential equations, equations involving ordinary p-Laplacians;
* monotone operators, nonlinear differential operators;
* difference equations in Hilbert spaces, including proximal point algorithms;
* the Fourier method for solving abstract evolution equations;
* optimization, input identifiability, [[optimal control]];
* applications in acoustics, capillarity theory, diffusion processes, fluid flows, hydraulics, integrated circuits, mathematical biology and ecology, nonlinear oscillators, phase field equations, self-organized systems, telegraph systems, etc.

In 1983 he was awarded the ''Gheorghe Lazăr'' Prize of the Romanian Academy in recognition of his outstanding contributions to the theory of hyperbolic partial differential equations.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://jurnalul.ro/special-jurnalul/reportaje/100-000-de-veghe-sub-rafturi-volume-seminarul-al-myller-din-iasi-cea-mai-mare-biblioteca-de-matematica-din-romania-si-din-estul-europei-682525.html|title=100.000 de veghe sub rafturi (volume). Seminarul Al. Myller din Iasi, cea mai veche biblioteca de matematica din Romania si din Estul Europei (in Romanian)|date=December 16, 2014|access-date=March 25, 2015|publisher=[[jurnalul.ro]]|author=Popa, C.C.|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150322014216/http://jurnalul.ro/special-jurnalul/reportaje/100-000-de-veghe-sub-rafturi-volume-seminarul-al-myller-din-iasi-cea-mai-mare-biblioteca-de-matematica-din-romania-si-din-estul-europei-682525.html|archive-date=March 22, 2015|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.momentul.ro/Momentul%20de%20Darabani/2010-11-15/Gheorghe+Morosanu++portret+sentimental |title=Gheorghe Moroșanu portret sentimental (in Romanian) |date=November 15, 2010 |accessdate=April 5, 2015 |publisher=momentul.ro |author=Teișanu, V. |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141223064910/http://www.momentul.ro/Momentul%20de%20Darabani/2010-11-15/Gheorghe+Morosanu++portret+sentimental |archivedate=December 23, 2014 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.stiri.botosani.ro/stire/66295/GHEORGHE+MORO%C5%9EANU%3A+%22Non-valoarea+este+agresiv%C4%83+%C5%9Fi+greu+de+%C3%AEnl%C4%83turat.+Va+fi+vina+noastr%C4%83+dac%C4%83+nu+facem+ceva+%C3%AEn+aceast%C4%83+direc%C5%A3ie!%22.html|title=Non-valoarea este agresivă și greu de inlăturat. Va fi vina noastră dacă nu facem ceva în această direcție (in Romanian)|date=March 13, 2014|accessdate=March 25, 2015|publisher=stiri.botosani.ro|author=Tonița, F.}}</ref> 
For the book of functional analysis mentioned above, Gheorghe Morosanu received in 2021 the ''Nicolae Teodorescu'' Prize from the [http://www.aosr.ro Academy of Romanian Scientists].

He holds ''Honorary Doctorates'' from the University of Craiova, Romania<ref>{{citation
| title = Gheorghe Moroșanu, Do we need mathematics?
| journal = Annals of the University of Craiova, Math. Comput. Sci. Series
| pages = 44 (2) (2017) 173–178}}</ref> and from the ''Ovidius'' University, Constanța, Romania.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://observator.ro/invatamant-titlul-de-doctor-honoris-causa-al-universitatii-ovidius-acordat-matematicianului-gh-morosanu-401006.html |title=Titlul de Doctor Honoris Causa al Universitatii Ovidius acordat matematicianului Gh. Morosanu |newspaper=Observator de Constanta |date=October 20, 2016 |language=ro |archive-url=https://archive.today/20161027102117/http://observator.ro/invatamant-titlul-de-doctor-honoris-causa-al-universitatii-ovidius-acordat-matematicianului-gh-morosanu-401006.html |archive-date=October 27, 2016 |accessdate=October 24, 2016 |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2019, he received the title of ''Professor Honoris Causa'' from the ''Babeș-Bolyai'' University, Cluj-Napoca, Romania<ref>[http://www.cs.ubbcluj.ro/doctori-si-profesori-honoris-causa Doctors and Professors Honoris Causa], retrieved May 5, 2019</ref>

A school (in Darabani) Gheorghe Moroșanu himself attended between 1957 and 1965 has been named after him since 2007, when he also received the title of ''Honorary Citizen'' of Darabani in recognition of his accomplishments.<ref>[http://www.isjbotosani.ro/img/uploads/carmen.tilica/file/Retea%20scolara%20Botosai-PJ+structuri-2014-2015.pdf List of Schools 2014-2015, Ministry of National Education, Botoșani County (Romania); see page 34, line 181] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150413111344/http://www.isjbotosani.ro/img/uploads/carmen.tilica/file/Retea%20scolara%20Botosai-PJ+structuri-2014-2015.pdf |date=2015-04-13 }}, retrieved April 4, 2015</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.stiri.botosani.ro/stire/22822/GHEORGHE+MOROSANU+-+Profesorul+caruia+orasul+natal+i-a+daruit+o+scoala!.html|title=Gheorghe Moroșanu - Profesorul căruia orașul natal i-a dăruit o școală (in Romanian)|date=September 9, 2010|accessdate=April 5, 2015|publisher=stiri.botosani.ro|author=stiri.botosani.ro}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.darabaneni.ro/scoala-gheorghe-morosanua-t257.html|title=Satul Teioasa are o poziție specială pe harta lumii... Teioasa nu mai e acolo, Teioasa e atunci (in Romanian)|date=March 15, 2014|accessdate=April 5, 2015|publisher=darabaneni.ro|author=Tonița, F.}}</ref><ref>[http://www.primariadarabani.ro/cetateni_de_onoare.php Gheorghe Moroșanu honorary citizen of Darabani] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150412155127/http://www.primariadarabani.ro/cetateni_de_onoare.php |date=2015-04-12 }}, retrieved April 5, 2015</ref>

In 2020 he became a ''Corresponding Member'' of the ''Academy of Romanian Scientists'', then ''Full Member'' in 2022.

In 2025 Gheorghe Moroșanu was awarded the title of ''Professor Emeritus'' of the ''Alexandru Ioan Cuza'' University of Iași, and in 2026 he became a ''Corresponding Member'' of the ''Accademia Peloritana dei Pericolanti'', Messina, Italia.
